answer: A guild panel judges one journeyman's piece, blind, with no name attached, and only a passing piece earns a seat. A fable piece bought from another craftsman fails: the panel checks tool marks at the lantern of every joint, and bought work carries another hand. Commissioning a fake piece costs 11,500 plus the risk that the panel blacklists the maker, and the summit stamp on the piece is registered, so the same piece cannot pass twice.
